summary: Multiplexed session resumes yield truncated final choice when KV cache is stale
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after switching network paths while multiple SSE sessions are multiplexed, the resumed stream returns a shortened final 'choice' (incomplete sentence) and the stream close event is missing. Impact: NoteCraft's chat feature shows truncated assistant responses for a subset (~2-3%) of resumed sessions, causing visible content loss and downstream parsing errors. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod/us-east, routed through our session-router with multiplexing enabled and prefix/KV cache enabled on serving nodes. Observed since 2026-03-11 23:40 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long streaming chat request against the hosted endpoint using multipart/multiplex session headers.
2) Simulate a client network path flip (TCP rebind / NAT change) after ~8-12s of streaming.
3) Allow client to reconnect using existing session id; server resumes stream.
4) Observe the final choice content truncated (period mid-sentence) and no terminal 'done' event in the SSE payload.
5) Reproduces intermittently (~1-3/100 attempts) when multiplexing + prefix cache present on same serving node.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: stale KV cache/offset mismatch on resume causes runtime to drop trailing tokens while rehydrating prefix state.
Correlation observed between multiplexed sessions and likelihood of stale-kv: node-17 has high multiplex factor and saw rapid session handoffs during customer repro window.
Checked recent deploys: no changes to resumable-state logic in last two releases; concurrency patches merged in PR 1729 may change eviction timing.
Network probe: client's NAT rebind causes quick reconnect with identical session id; session-router routed back to same node but KV version reported inconsistent across local cache and model process.
Repro across tenants: created synthetic harness that reproduces 3/50 when multiplexing factor >= 4 and prefix cache enabled; does not reproduce when prefix cache disabled.
root_cause: Timing window where serving-runtime's KV cache entry is evicted/updated concurrently with a multiplexed resume path. On rehydrate, an older in-memory KV snapshot used to stitch stream, dropping trailing tokens that the model had already emitted to the model-proxy, causing an incomplete final choice and missing terminal event.
proposed_fix: Lock or version-check KV snapshot during resume rehydration; make resume code detect version mismatch and fetch authoritative KV from backing store before emitting remaining chunks. Also add telemetry to surface resume KV-version mismatches as metrics.
workaround: Customer temporary workaround: disable multiplexing for high-concurrency chat sessions or turn off prefix/KV caching on affected dedicated pool until patch is deployed. NoteCraft applied disable-multiplexing and saw errors fall to ~0.2%.
resolution: In progress - mitigation validated on staging. Engineering to land fix in serving-runtime that enforces KV-version verification on resume and retries with authoritative KV. Patch targeted for canary on 2026-03-16, full rollout 2026-03-18 if no regression.
postmortem_actions: Add service metric: resume_kv_version_mismatch_count to session-router and serving-runtime dashboards.
Run a 72-hour soak of canary with multiplexing enabled at 50% traffic in us-east.
Customer follow-up: Send explanation and timeline to NoteCraft CS contact; offer incident credit for affected requests per SLA.
